chapter: Ch. 4 (The Anatomy of an AI Workload), sidebar table
evidence: Sidebar row label reads "Cloud, 6 hosts — default paid-occupancy input" for the $87,600 / ≈$14.04 per-1K-request line, but the reconciliation on p.91 states the opposite default: "The default rented-fleet unit-cost figure to quote (average traffic, hour-matched basis): (c) ~$0.0033 per request (≈$3.33 per 1K)". The same table cell then says "quote ≈$3.33/1K instead".
issue: Two competing "defaults" for the same 6-host fleet are printed in the same chapter: the table labels the 730-hour paid-occupancy line "default", while the reconciliation paragraph designates the hour-matched $3.33/1K line as the default unit cost. A reader skimming the sidebar can quote $14.04/1K as the default, which the chapter elsewhere calls an "hour-basis artifact".
fix_instruction: Relabel the sidebar row to "Cloud, 6 hosts — 730-hour paid-occupancy input (hour-basis artifact)" and reserve the word "default" for the $3.33/1K hour-matched row, so the table and the §4.3 reconciliation use one designation.

evidence: Page 27 cites the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next context window as "Appendix A §10", while page 51 cites the same model card as "(source: model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10)".
issue: Two different reference forms ("Appendix A §10" and "A.10") point at the same appendix location, and neither matches the appendix's own stated numbering convention from the Preface ("Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N"). Under that convention "A.10" reads as a figure, but the List of Figures stops at A.5.
fix_instruction: Pick one form for appendix sections (the Preface's letter-suffix form, e.g. "§ 10A", or a plain "A §10") and apply it at both page 27 and page 51; do not use the A.N figure-style token for a section.

evidence: Table 6-1's Decode row puts the verdict in a column headed "H100 capacity" containing "~3.35 TB/s HBM (single-device)" and a "Verdict" cell that says "memory-bound by intensity (~1.0 FLOP/byte ≪ ridge ~295); weight-read bandwidth is not binding at the canonical point — 0.70 TB/s ÷ 3.35 TB/s = 20.9% achieved HBM util".
issue: The table's own verdict column simultaneously asserts "memory-bound" and "weight-read bandwidth is not binding" without flagging that these are two different senses of the word (roofline regime vs. achieved-utilization shortfall). The same cell carries both a batch-1 single-device signature and the TP=8 host signature, which is the exact conflation the chapter's §6.3.3 prose warns against ("This 5.6-vs-3.35 TB/s comparison is an illustrative single-device roofline argument, not the canonical 8×H100 host's actual deployment verdict").
fix_instruction: Split the Decode verdict cell into two explicitly named rows or sub-rows — "regime (roofline)" and "achieved HBM utilization on the canonical host" — and state in the cell that the 5.6-vs-3.35 TB/s comparison applies to the hypothetical single-device case only.

evidence: The figure box prints "Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency", and the caption concedes: "the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric."
issue: A known erratum is shipped in the figure and corrected only in the caption. §6.1.1 and Ch. 4 §4.3 both insist concurrency is a derived serving-side quantity, so the figure contradicts the chapter's own taxonomy on its first page.
fix_instruction: Re-render Fig. 6.1 with the workload box reading "rps (λ) · token profile" only, and delete the caption erratum note once the art is corrected.

evidence: The sidebar table states: "capex amortized: 21 × ($350K capex [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.3333 + $1,110.33 energy [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff (Ch 16)". The displayed bracket expression does not arithmetically sum to the displayed total: 21 × ($5,833.3333 + $1,110.33) + $10,000 = 21 × $6,943.6633 + $10,000 = $145,816.93 + $10,000 = $155,816.93 only if you use un-rounded per-host values. But 21 × ($5,833.33 + $1,110.33) + $10,000 = 21 × $6,943.66 + $10,000 = $145,816.86 + $10,000 = $155,816.86 ≠ $155,816.93. The 7-cent discrepancy means the displayed per-host figures, when summed as shown, do not produce the printed total.
issue: The bracket expression uses rounded per-host values ($5,833.33 + $1,110.33 = $6,943.66) that yield $155,816.86 when multiplied by 21 and summed with $10,000, not the stated $155,816.93. The total is only correct if computed from un-rounded intermediates, but the displayed formula as written is off by $0.07.
fix_instruction: Either round the total to match the displayed intermediate values ($155,816.86), or show more precision in the per-host figures (e.g. $1,110.3259), or add a parenthetical note that the total is computed from un-rounded intermediates.

evidence: Section §1.5 Common Mistakes: "Ignoring the input/output asymmetry. Treating a request as 'one unit' hides that input-heavy workloads tend toward high prefill compute and KV-capacity pressure, while output-heavy ones are decode-dominant (run-time per generated token) — opposite bottlenecks with opposite fixes." The parenthetical "(run-time per generated token)" glosses "decode-dominant" but introduces a third name ("run-time") that does not appear in the book's defined terminology elsewhere, where decode is consistently described as "bandwidth-bound" or by TPOT.
issue: The phrase 'run-time per generated token' introduces an ad-hoc synonym for decode cost that conflicts with the book's established terminology (TPOT, decode bandwidth-bound). A reader tracing this term elsewhere will not find it defined.
fix_instruction: Replace '(run-time per generated token)' with the book's standard term, e.g. '(TPOT × output length)' or '(per-token decode cost)'.

evidence: Preface, Reading conventions, Cross-references: "A section reference takes the form § N.M ... which means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4". However §7.3 appears at page 136 (Ch 7 opening) as "the whole-slot floor of 17 KV-resident requests" and at page 137 as "The canonical concurrency ceiling is that resident-basis quotient floored to a whole slot — 17" — neither instance is preceded by an explicit 'Ch. 7 §' within the same sentence. The convention says bare §N.M 'names Chapter N, Section M' but §7.3 numerically means Ch 7, Section 3, which is the Worked Example section — the concurrency ceiling content actually lives in §7.3 as numbered. Reading §7.3 as 'Ch 7, Section 3' is correct; reading it as 'Section 7.3 of the current chapter' is also correct only because these instances are inside Ch 7.
issue: Bare '§7.3' references (pages 136, 145) do not include the chapter prefix 'Ch. 7' at first mention in those sentences, creating ambiguity with the Preface convention that '§ N.M' means Chapter N Section M (where §7.3 → Ch 7, Section 3, not section 7.3 of an unknown chapter). The instances are unambiguous only because they occur within Ch 7 itself.
fix_instruction: At first mention within each chapter, write 'Ch. 7 § 3' instead of bare '§7.3' to avoid ambiguity, per the Preface's own stated convention.

evidence: Page 86, latency bullet: "budget of 1.2 s, comprising retrieval (~120 ms for vector search and reranking on a local GPU) + prefill (budget cap 1.08 s for 9,200 tokens across the 8×H100 canonical host — a budget, not a modeled runtime." The sentence uses an opening parenthesis for the prefill term but the parenthetical is never closed on that line — it continues across multiple sentences including "The cap implies ≈8,500 tokens/s..." and "The minimum GPU count..." before the bullet ends with ") Per Ch 2 and Ch 8)." — a double closing parenthesis with no matching double opening. The sentence structure makes the prefill parenthetical span ~15 sentences, which is difficult to track.
issue: The prefill parenthetical opens with a single '(' but closes with '))' at the end of the bullet, and spans an extremely long run of text (multiple sentences about GPU counts, MFU, and capacity screens). This makes the parenthetical structure unbalanced and hard to follow.
fix_instruction: Break the long parenthetical into a separate sentence or a footnote; ensure parentheses are balanced (one open matches one close).

evidence: Table 3-3 — Parameter and KV cache arithmetic: dense 70B vs MoE (8×7B class) lists the row "KV cache per request (9.2K ctx, FP16)" with the MoE column value "~1.2 GB" and derivation "9,200 × 0.131 MB/token ≈ 1.20 GB". But the same chapter's §3.3.3 text states: "KV per token = 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 = 65,536 B = 0.0655 MB/token at 8-bit, so 9,200 × 0.0655 MB ≈ 0.60 GB (≈1.2 GB at FP16)". The derivation in Table 3-3 says 0.131 MB/token, which is the FP16 rate, but the text immediately above it labels 0.0655 MB/token as the 8-bit rate and 1.2 GB as the FP16 figure — so the table row's per-token constant (0.131 MB) is FP16, not 8-bit, while the neighbouring 8-bit row derives 0.0655 MB from the same geometry. Both are internally consistent per-row, but a reader scanning the two rows sees 0.131 MB and 0.0655 MB for what the text calls the same 'challenger's own 32L/4096H GQA (8 KV-heads × 128)' geometry without the table stating that 0.131 is the FP16 figure and 0.0655 the 8-bit figure; the row labels carry the precision, so this is a presentation-clarity defect rather than an arithmetic error.
issue: Table 3-3's two KV rows for the MoE column use per-token constants (0.131 MB vs 0.0655 MB) that differ by exactly 2x (FP16 vs 8-bit) but the table does not label the precision of the per-token constant in the derivation cell, unlike Table 7-1 which explicitly states '8-bit here means FP8 (one byte per K/V element), not a block-scaled INT8 scale-offset layout'.
fix_instruction: In Table 3-3, add the precision qualifier to each per-token constant in the derivation cells (e.g. '0.131 MB/token at FP16' and '0.0655 MB/token at 8-bit, raw byte-halving'), matching the labelling discipline already used in Table 7-1 and in the §3.3.3 prose.

evidence: Section 2.3 states the canonical-host verdict: "prefill 1.29 PFLOP / (8 × 0.989 PFLOPS) = 0.16 s at peak, ~0.47 s at 35% MFU". Chapter 4 §4.3 repeats: "The modelled host prefill is ~0.16 s at peak and ~0.47 s at 35% MFU (Ch 2)". Chapter 6 §6.3.3 uses the same: "the 8×H100 sustained prefill capacity of ~2.77 PFLOP/s (35% MFU, Ch 8 §3)". But Chapter 4 §4.3 also states the implied single-request rate as: "The cap implies ≈8,500 tokens/s (9,200 ÷ 1.08 = 8,519): that is only the budget-implied single-request rate for a request that holds the whole host". Chapter 4 then computes "the 8-GPU host needs ~0.47 s (9,200 ÷ 19,780 = 0.465 s; 19,780 = 8 × 2,472.5 tok/s, the unrounded form of the ~19,800 tok/s planning rate)". So the same host is credited with both ~8,500 tok/s (budget-implied, ~1.08 s) and ~19,780 tok/s (35% MFU planning rate, ~0.47 s) — the book labels the 8,500 figure as 'only the budget-implied single-request rate for a request that holds the whole host' and warns not to divide by it. The two rates are distinguished in prose but appear on the same page of Ch 4 without a shared 'do not compare' warning at the point where the ~19,800 tok/s planning rate is itself used as a fleet-sizing denominator (Chapter 4 §4.6: 'prefill screens at ≥5 hosts at average (92,000 ÷ 19,800 = 4.65, ceiled)' and the mini-case at §4.8: '50 rps × 9,200 input = 460,000 prefill tokens/s ÷ ~19,800 tokens/s per host ... = 24 hosts').
issue: Two materially different prefill rates for the same 8×H100 host (~8,500 tok/s budget-implied and ~19,800 tok/s at 35% MFU) coexist in Ch 4 §4.3 within a few paragraphs; the first is explicitly flagged as not-a-host-rate but the second is then used as a per-host fleet-sizing denominator in §4.6 and §4.8 without repeating the warning that it is a planning rate, not a measured or SLO-goodput rate.
fix_instruction: At the point in §4.6 and §4.8 where ~19,800 tok/s is used as the per-host prefill denominator, restate in-line that this is the 35% MFU sustained-planning rate (a planning bound, not a measured goodput), and note the contrast with the ~8,500 tok/s budget-implied single-request rate so the two are not conflated by a reader scanning the chapter.

evidence: The §4.8 mini-case states: "the normative host-count form of Ch 17 Table 17-1 gives ⌈26 ÷ 0.70⌉ = ⌈37.14⌉ = 38 hosts (the occupancy cross-check ⌈430/(17 × 0.7)⌉ = ⌈430/11.9⌉ = ⌈36.13⌉ = 37 sits one host below it) — then 39 hosts before the spare, 40 under the book's provisioning policy, which multiplies the independent ρ = 0.95 as well and adds the N−1 reserve (⌈430/(17 × 0.70 × 0.95)⌉ = ⌈430/11.305⌉ = ⌈38.04⌉ = 39; Ch 17 Table 17-1 adds +1 for the N−1 spare → 40). The same total by the host-count form: with N full-utilization hosts, total (provisioned) = ⌈N ÷ (u × ρ)⌉ = ⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ and working = total − 1 — here N = ⌈430/17⌉ = 26, so ⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ = ⌈39.10⌉ = 40 provisioned, 39 working." Two different derivations are given for the same 40/39 answer, and the second (the normative one) is presented as 'the same total by the host-count form'. Recomputing: 430/17 = 25.294 → N = 26; 26 ÷ 0.665 = 39.098 → ⌈39.098⌉ = 40; working = 40 − 1 = 39. ✓ The first path: 430/(17 × 0.70 × 0.95) = 430/11.305 = 38.036 → ⌈38.036⌉ = 39, then +1 = 40. ✓ Both reach 40/39, but the passage also states that the occupancy cross-check 'is a bound, not a reproduction of the provisioned total' — which is true at the 37-vs-38 stage, but the 39-vs-40 stage does reproduce it exactly, and the text presents the two as 'two forms' of the same rule while one is declared a cross-check. The prose requires the reader to track four different ceilings (37, 38, 39, 40) with different labels.
issue: The mini-case derives the same 40-host/39-working fleet answer twice through two different arithmetic paths (⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ = 40 and ⌈430/11.305⌉ = 39 +1 = 40) while simultaneously declaring one of those paths a non-normative 'cross-check' that 'sits one host below' the normative result — a claim true only at the u-only stage, not at the policy stage where the two agree exactly.
fix_instruction: In §4.8, either present only the normative host-count form (⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ = 40 provisioned, 39 working) and state the occupancy form once as a bound, or make explicit that at the policy stage the two forms coincide at 40, so the reader is not left with an unqualified 'one host below' statement that the same paragraph's arithmetic contradicts.

evidence: Section 6.3.4 reads: "aggregate prefill demand at the 40 rps peak is 40 × 1.29 ≈ 51.6 PFLOP/s against the 8×H100 sustained prefill capacity of ~2.77 PFLOP/s (35% MFU, Ch 8 §3) — ~18.6× oversubscribed (the datasheet-peak ~7.9 PFLOPS gives ~6.5×, a theoretical ceiling only; under case (ii), full-square attention, the same 40 rps traffic peak at the same 35% MFU planning rate screens ~22 hosts — Ch 8 §3), consistent with Ch 8's 19-host screen at this peak (case (i))". The §6.8 mini-case then states: "case (i)'s prefill screen needs ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts, but the KV-residency / Little's-Law screen needs ⌈344/17⌉ = 21 hosts at the peak and therefore binds (Ch 8 §3; Ch 17)". The host reference 'Ch 8 §3' is therefore used for four distinct quantities in two chapters — the 19-host case-(i) screen, the ~22-host case-(ii) screen, the ~2.77 PFLOP/s capacity figure, and the 35% MFU planning rate — with no figure or table number given for any of them, even though Chapter 8's Table 8-1 is the natural anchor for the prefill rate and the case-(i)/(ii)/(iii) convention is defined in Ch 2 Table 2-2's scope note and Ch 8 §3.3.
issue: Cross-references to 'Ch 8 §3' are used as the sole authority for four different numeric results across Ch 6 (§6.3.4 and §6.8), including a 19-host screen, a 22-host screen, a 2.77 PFLOP/s capacity and a 35% MFU planning rate, with no figure/table pointer — so a reader cannot verify which specific artefact carries each number without reading all of Ch 8 §3.
fix_instruction: Give each of the four Ch 8-sourced quantities in §6.3.4 and §6.8 a specific pointer (e.g. 'Ch 8 §3, Table 8-1' for the ~2.77 PFLOP/s planning capacity and the 35% MFU assumption, and 'Ch 8 §3 case (i) / case (ii)' for the 19- and 22-host screens), so the referenced targets can be resolved individually.

evidence: Table 4-2's canonical-scenario ledger row "Execution occupancy" gives "~86 / ~344 requests (at Wexec ≈ 8.6 s, where Wexec = 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode = 8.58 s, shown as 8.6 s throughout the book; upper bound — Wexec contains the 1.08 s two-term prefill cap, so B_other is not deducted)". §4.3's Canonical Workload box repeats "Mean request service time (planning headline — not used for occupancy) ~10 s" and the execution-occupancy note: "The occupancy service time is Wexec ≈ 8.6 s: prefill + decode, shown as 8.58 s in Table 4-2. It excludes the ~120 ms retrieval term." Chapter 2 §2.3 states the same occupancy: "the capacity question — how many such hosts to absorb λ = 40 rps, where in-flight concurrency Lexec = λWexec ≈344 at the ~8.6 s service time (that occupancy is derived in Ch 4 §3 and carried in Table 4-2)". Recomputing: 40 rps × 8.58 s = 343.2 → ~344 ✓; 10 rps × 8.58 s = 85.8 → ~86 ✓. But Chapter 4 §4.6 uses the per-host slot screen as '86 in-flight ÷ 17 slots = 5.06' and Chapter 17's host count ⌈344/17⌉ = 21. With Wexec shown as '8.6 s' in the ledger and '8.58 s' in the prose, a reader recomputing 40 × 8.6 = 344 exactly, and one recomputing 40 × 8.58 = 343.2, get the same headline; however Chapter 4 §4.3's own cost-basis arithmetic elsewhere in the chapter uses a distinct third number: 'the same fleet is ~$3.33 per 1K requests (hour-matched, active-hours basis, 6-host average at the ~10 rps average)' derived from '10 × 3,600 × 8 × 260/12 = 6,240,000' — while the per-request decode figure quoted repeatedly for the same workload is '300 × 25 ms = 7.5 s'. The 8.58 s figure therefore embeds the 1.08 s prefill cap (which Table 4-2 flags as 'NOT a feasible deployed prefill target', since budget_prefill ≤ 1.08 s − B_other), so every occupancy, host-count and $/1K figure in Chs 4, 6, 8, 16, 17 and 20 inherits an upper-bound service time that the book itself says cannot be met in deployment.
issue: The service time Wexec = 8.58 s used as the denominator for every Little's-law occupancy, host-count and per-1K-request figure book-wide is built on the 1.08 s prefill figure that Table 4-2 explicitly labels 'two-term-only upper cap, NOT a feasible deployed prefill target' with 'B_other' (admission/queue and tokenization/transfer) not deducted; the upper-bound status is noted on the Table 4-2 row and in the Canonical Workload box, but the derived occupancies (~86/~344), the 17-slot host screen (⌈344/17⌉ = 21) and the cost-per-1K figures do not repeat it, so a reader can carry them into a sizing deck as measured quantities.
fix_instruction: Add the 'upper-bound, B_other not deducted' qualifier inline to the execution-occupancy row's downstream consumers — at minimum where ~86/~344 is first used for the 17-slot host screen in §4.6 and where the host counts are quoted in the §4.8 mini-case — so the inherited bound travels with the numbers rather than only with the Table 4-2 source row.

chapter: Ch 3, §3.6.1 'Why the trend signal should not be read as "dense is dead"'
evidence: "Qwen3.8-27B ([1P][FACT], model card: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B is a dense 27.8B model whose 4-bit weights fit on a single 24 GB consumer GPU, and Muse Glimmer 30B ([2°][FACT], source: vLLM-Recipes, citing the Meta model card) is a dense 29.6B local-agentic model..."
issue: Unbalanced parenthesis: the '(' opened after 'Qwen3.8-27B' is never closed, so the source-citation parenthetical swallows the main clause ('is a dense 27.8B model...'). The parallel construction for 'Muse Glimmer 30B (...)' closes its parenthesis before 'is a dense 29.6B', confirming the intended closure point after the URL.
fix_instruction: Insert the closing parenthesis after the model-card URL: 'Qwen3.8-27B ([1P][FACT], model card: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) is a dense 27.8B model...'.

evidence: Figure art text layer prints: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". The caption states the line is "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget". Ch 4 (printed p. 86) is emphatic: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to".
issue: The art labels the 2 s line '(TTFT budget)', contradicting the book's load-bearing budget-vs-ceiling terminology (1.2 s = design budget; 2 s = p95 ceiling). The caption corrects the semantics but never acknowledges that the art itself carries the wrong term, so a reader of the figure alone internalizes exactly the conflation the Preface forbids ('load-bearing contrasts are never relaxed').
fix_instruction: Relabel the figure's SLO line to 'SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)' (or 'p95 ceiling ≤ 2 s'); caption can then stand unchanged.

evidence: Art text layer: "Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency". §6.1.1: "Concurrency is not a workload input: it is a serving-side quantity derived from the arrival rate and the time in system (Little's law)... Fig 6.1's workload box therefore carries only offered quantities — the request rate λ (rps) and the token profile." Caption: "the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric."
issue: The workload box of the chapter's spine figure prints 'concurrency' as a workload metric, contradicting §6.1.1's classification (concurrency is serving-side, derived like queue depth). The caption admits the erratum, but the shipped art still carries the wrong label, so figure and body text disagree.
fix_instruction: Correct the figure art: replace the third entry 'concurrency' with 'request rate λ' (or delete it) so the box matches §6.1.1; the caption's erratum note can then be removed.

evidence: "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the schematic is drawn from the documented mechanism ([1P][FACT]: the per-token K/V accounting of the DeepSeek-V2 MLA report, arXiv:2405.04434), and the 64-head geometry it abbreviates carries that same label ([canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], Ch. 4, Table 4-2), not a vendor checkpoint"
issue: Ambiguous, self-contradictory label referent: 'that same label' grammatically points to the figure's own [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] tag, but the parenthetical assigns [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] — two different Axis-1 provenances under the book's own taxonomy (Table 4-2 Note 1: '[canonical scenario] is distinct from [ILLUSTRATIVE]'). The reader cannot determine which label the 64-head geometry actually carries.
fix_instruction: Reword to '...and the 64-head geometry it abbreviates carries its own label ([canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], Ch. 4, Table 4-2)' so the figure tag and the geometry tag are no longer conflated by 'that same label'.

chapter: Ch 1 §1.1.2 / Ch 3 §3.6.1 vs Preface cross-reference convention (printed p. xix)
evidence: Preface convention: "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N." Ch 1 (printed p. 3): "...all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10". Ch 3 (printed p. 51): "(source: model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10)".
issue: Three mutually inconsistent forms for appendix pointers: the stated convention (letter-suffixed sections, e.g. §9A; figures A.N), an unsuffixed 'Appendix A §10', and a bare 'A.10' that collides with the appendix's figure-numbering form (List of Figures shows only A.1–A.5, so 'A.10' cannot be a figure and is not a well-formed section reference either). At least one of the three is wrong, and the targets cannot be confirmed to resolve.
fix_instruction: Adopt one section form (e.g. 'Appendix A §10A' or, if unsuffixed sections exist, 'Appendix A §10'), amend the Preface convention sentence accordingly, and replace the bare 'A.10' on printed p. 51 with the full section form.

evidence: Table 6-1, Decode row, Resource tell column: "(ii) Canonical 8×H100, TP=8 operating point: low-to-moderate HBM util (~21% of 3.35 TB/s), so HBM saturation is not the tell here"
issue: The resource tell for the canonical host in Table 6-1 incorrectly lists low HBM utilization as a diagnostic signal for a memory-bound regime. Low utilization is a symptom of the tensor-parallel sharding (where the weight read is distributed), not an indicator of the underlying roofline regime (memory-bound). This contradicts the text in §2.3 and §6.3.3, which explicitly state that the bandwidth-bound verdict comes from arithmetic intensity (~1 FLOP/byte), not from the device utilization rate. A reader looking for high HBM utilization to confirm 'memory-bound' on an 8xH100 host will not find it.
fix_instruction: Clarify that 'low HBM util' is an artifact of the TP=8 distribution, and that the 'tell' for this regime on the canonical host is actually the high ratio of memory-read latency to compute time, or TP-collective overhead, rather than the raw bandwidth percentage. Alternatively, restrict this 'tell' to the single-device hypothetical row to avoid confusion.

evidence: §2.1.2 'Implementation note inspected on 28 October 2026 (post-cutoff addendum...) ... The pinned source establishes the execution pattern below, not a measurement of latency, memory use or service capacity.'
issue: The book uses a future date (2026) for a 'post-cutoff addendum' in a section describing a specific implementation inspection. While consistent with the fictional future edition of the book, the phrase 'outside the 30 August 2026 evidence snapshot' combined with the specific date '28 October 2026' introduces a temporal inconsistency in the document's own 'current time' if not carefully read, as it describes an event happening after the 'First edition, 2026' publication date listed on the title page.
fix_instruction: Add a footnote or clarification that the '2026' dates refer to the book's fictional 'current era' context, or verify that the 'First edition 2026' date on the cover implies these are post-publication updates. (Note: This is likely intentional world-building for the AI persona, but technically flagged as a temporal anomaly in a static document).

chapter: Chapter 6 — Measuring What Matters: From Telemetry to Architecture Decisions
evidence: Figure art: "Workload metrics rps · token profile · concurrency". Caption: "Figure-art note: the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric."
issue: The rendered figure still labels concurrency as a workload metric, while §6.1.1 and the caption state that concurrency is derived on the serving side and the offered request rate λ belongs in the workload box. This is a figure-versus-text mismatch visible to readers.
fix_instruction: Regenerate Figure 6.1 so the workload box reads "rps · token profile · λ" (or equivalent offered-load wording), remove "concurrency" from that box, and then delete the now-unnecessary figure-art erratum note from the caption.
